extraction.name: Challenging BIG-Bench tasks and whether chain-of-thought can solve them
extraction.description: Paper introducing BIG-Bench Hard (BBH), a curated subset of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks, and evaluating answer-only versus chain-of-thought prompting on language models.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors curated BIG-Bench Hard by filtering BIG-Bench tasks using criteria such as number of subtasks, number of examples, availability of human-rater baselines, evaluation metric, prior model performance, and task scope. They manually wrote chain-of-thought exemplars for each BBH task and publicly released the data, prompts, and Codex outputs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some BIG-Bench tasks lacked human baselines or had incomplete metadata; the paper notes that tasks vary in how clean their data and metadata are.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: BIG-Bench tasks and their associated examples, prompts, human-rater baselines, and model evaluation outputs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Tasks were filtered according to explicit criteria: removing tasks with more than three subtasks, fewer than 103 examples, no human-rater baseline, non-multiple-choice/non-exact-match metrics, tasks where prior best model beat average human-rater score, and tasks deemed outside the scope of the work. For BBH, random subsets of 250 evaluation examples were taken for all but three tasks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering and curation of BIG-Bench tasks to produce a clean subset of 23 tasks; for most tasks, sampling 250 evaluation examples; using exact match accuracy and greedy decoding for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: BIG-Bench organizers enlisted human raters to manually solve tasks and score them against golden labels to establish human-rater baselines. The authors manually composed three chain-of-thought exemplars for each BBH task.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human-rater scores are described as not fully representative of human performance and should be interpreted with care. The paper compares average and maximum human-rater performance against model outputs and notes that some tasks still lag expert human-rater performance.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The data, prompts, and Codex model outputs are publicly available at the project GitHub repository. No further versioning, update schedule, maintainers, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper notes that some tasks involve moral judgment scenarios and that delegating agency to models about moral judgment was avoided. It also cautions that surpassing average human-rater performance should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human-rater scores are not representative of the entire population. Some tasks require knowledge or presuppositions rooted in Western society, and the benchmark includes tasks with potential ambiguity or domain-specific difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Human-rater baselines may not represent the full population; some tasks are extremely difficult, ambiguous, or require specialized knowledge; answer-only prompting can underestimate model capabilities; BBH is limited to tasks with multiple-choice or exact-match evaluation and mostly uses 250 sampled evaluation examples per task.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of language models using few-shot prompting and chain-of-thought prompting; benchmarking and analysis of model capabilities on challenging reasoning tasks; publicly released for further research.
